title: Token energy tradeoffs: A10 / L4 / A100 / H100 (working notes)
body:
Quick summary:
These are working notes for a compact per-token / perf-per-watt comparison across A10, L4, A100, and H100 for a medium-sized generation workload (single-sequence autoregressive sampling; top-k/top-p disabled) using a 13B family model equivalent with KV cache enabled. Numbers below are from short microbench runs (see linked artifacts) and rough cloud-seat cost assumptions — treat as order-of-magnitude for tradeoffs, not final billing.

Assumptions / measurement notes:
- Model: synthetic 13B transformer (dense) with standard attention; 2048 context used for throughput runs.
- Sequence generation workload: steady-state streaming generation at 1 token per step latencies measured; batch sizes swept (1, 4, 16).
- Power numbers are measured average GPU board power under load (approx), not PUE or host CPU power.
- Hourly list prices are representative reserved-on-demand analogs used solely for relative $/token estimates.
- Measurements done on separate days; variance ~±8–12% typical.

Summary table (working numbers):
GPU   | hourly($) | avg power(W) | tok/s (batch=4) | tok/s/W | $/token (micro)
------|-----------|--------------|-----------------|---------|---------------
A10   | 0.90      | 150          | 180             | 1.20    | 0.00000139    
L4    | 1.50      | 150          | 320             | 2.13    | 0.00000130    
A100  | 3.80      | 350          | 920             | 2.63    | 0.00000115    
H100  | 7.20      | 700          | 1600            | 2.29    | 0.00000125    

Notes on table calculations (how these were derived):
- tok/s/W = (tok/s) / (power(W)).  Example: L4 = 320 / 150 = 2.13 tok/s/W.
- $/token = hourly($) / (tok/s * 3600).  Example: A100 = 3.8 / (920*3600) ≈ 1.15e-6 $/token.
- All token rates are for generation-only (no heavy sampling temperature overhead). Latency tail behavior differs: A10/L4 show longer tails under small batches.

Interpretation / tradeoffs:
- Lowest absolute $/token in our runs: A100 (best raw $/token) thanks to high throughput. H100 is close but more expensive per-hour so slightly worse $/token in this regime.
- Perf/W: A100 shows best perf-per-watt in this specific microbenchmark, but L4 is competitive and much cheaper to spin up; for moderate scale, L4 becomes attractive because of lower absolute commit and simpler autoscaling.
- A10 is useful for very low-cost, low-throughput use cases (small experiments, dev), but latency and tail variance are worse.
- H100 shines when single-GPU latency and burst throughput matter (very large batch or long-context models, FP16 kernels), and when model parallelism reduces idle cycles — but needs larger commitment and rack-level power considerations.

Operational recommendations (working):
1) For cost-sensitive batched workloads (embedding-heavy or high-throughput generation) prioritize A100-backed pools with aggressive quantization and batching. Keep L4 as a lower-commit alternative for medium traffic.
2) For latency-sensitive, low-concurrency endpoints (PLG front-ends), evaluate L4 + tuned batcher first — cost/latency sweet spot in many of our tests. Consider H100 only if single-request latencies at high QPS become dominant and you can amortize the per-hour cost.
3) Autoscaling: prefer mixing L4 + A100 pools with routing policy by SLO and cost: route to L4 by default, overflow to A100/H100 when queueing/backlog exceeds X ms.
4) Measurement hygiene: standardized microbench harness (see linked artifacts) with three canonical prompts: short (10 tokens), medium (100 tokens), long (1024 tokens). Capture p50/p95/p99, power draw, and tokens/sec for each.

Optimization levers to test next (experiment matrix):
- Quantization levels: int8 vs int4 (quality check on eval set) across all GPUs.
- KV cache reuse patterns for multi-call chats and large context reuse.
- Batching heuristics: dynamic vs fixed; measure latency tail impact.
- Mixed-instance routing: measure cost delta when routing 20/50/80% traffic to cheaper pools.

Open questions / risks:
- Our power readings exclude host-level overhead (CPU, NIC, PSUs), so perf/W numbers are GPU-board-only; real perf-per-watt at rack-level will be worse.
- Pricing assumptions vary by cloud region; reserved vs spot impacts decision.
- Models with sparse kernels / FSDP sharding may change A100/H100 relative rankings.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Run standardized microbench across 3 model sizes (7B,13B,70B) and store canonical results in the benchmarking repo (owner: Ethan).
- Add PUE-corrected perf/W rows (include host + networking) and recalc $/token with PUE=1.1 and host power approximations (owner: Maya).
- Draft a short one-pager for sales/solutions (what instance to recommend for X workload) with crisp SLO+cost rules (owner: Riley).

Notes-to-self: keep this as a lightweight working doc; final numbers get exported into the canonical sheet (Instance Benchmark Template). Expect revisions after larger batch runs and when int4 kernels are available on the L4/A10 builds.

References and quick links: see linked_artifacts above and the benchmarking PR for raw logs.

End of notes.
